title: Vancomycin
sources: Rybak MJ, Le J, Lodise TP, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections: A revised consensus guideline and review by ASHP, IDSA, PIDS, and SIDP. Am J Health Syst Pharm. 2020;77(11):835-864.

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (vancomycin appeared only by name inside empiric-antibiotic references, with no dosing card). New 'Antimicrobial Dosing' category added to Drug & Dosing since none previously existed for this drug class.

purpose: Empiric loading and starting maintenance dosing for a glycopeptide antibiotic covering MRSA and other gram-positive organisms — one of the most commonly needed critical-illness antibiotic doses, and one with real nephrotoxicity stakes if monitoring is skipped.

doses.indication: Loading dose — serious/critical infection (sepsis, meningitis, endocarditis)
doses.notes: Infuse over ≥ 1-2 h (rate ≤ 10 mg/min or per your institution's max concentration/rate policy) to reduce infusion-related reactions. Round to a practical dose your pharmacy stocks.

doses.indication: Maintenance dosing — empiric starting point pending levels

rule.repeat: Every 8-12 h in normal renal function; extend the interval as CrCl falls. This is an empiric STARTING point, not the final dose — actual maintenance dosing should be guided by levels.

doses.notes: Renal function drives the interval more than the per-dose amount — a patient with reduced CrCl gets the same per-kg dose less often, not routinely a smaller dose. AUC-guided dosing (target AUC24 400-600 mg·h/L assuming MIC 1) is the preferred monitoring strategy per the 2020 ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP consensus guideline — via Bayesian dosing software where available, or two-level PK sampling; trough-only monitoring (target 15-20 mg/L) is older and still common without Bayesian access, but tends to overshoot the AUC target and raise nephrotoxicity risk for the same apparent trough. Nephrotoxicity risk rises with AUC24 > 600, concurrent nephrotoxins (piperacillin-tazobactam co-administration specifically flagged across multiple studies), and pre-existing renal impairment — check and trend renal function during therapy. In renal impairment or CRRT/hemodialysis, dosing is highly protocol- and modality-specific — involve pharmacy beyond the empiric first dose.

contraindications: Known vancomycin anaphylaxis (true IgE-mediated allergy — distinct from vancomycin infusion reaction / 'red man syndrome', which is rate-related histamine release, not a true allergy, and is managed by slowing the infusion rather than avoiding the drug)
buildNote: Loading dose is a clean per-kg rule; maintenance dosing is deliberately framed as an empiric starting point rather than a precise computed number, since real maintenance dosing is AUC/level-guided, not a fixed formula — encoding a false-precision maintenance number would misrepresent current practice.
